correctness.rationale: Exact orthogonal sine/cosine decomposition gives the fixed-gap kernel and unique reproducing-kernel extremizer. The strict universal inequality follows from an explicit gap split and a sign-definite derivative F''(d)=4 sin(d)(sin(d)-d cos(d)); the latter is positive on (0,π). A separate elementary sine inequality controls all real x≥1. Taylor expansion yields the exact positive d² coefficient. The bundled script passed 448 supplementary assertions, not used as a substitute for infinite proof.

value.rationale: Sharp two-atom exterior leverage is a canonical minimal nontrivial instance of the current sparse-Fourier extrapolation problem. It yields an exact optimal constant and fixed-gap stability profile rather than an arbitrary finite experiment or renamed bound; the quadratic collision loss quantitatively measures how nearly degenerate real spectral atoms become worst-case for prediction, a useful benchmark for clustered-spectrum regression.
